title: Mark Ruffalo Escalates Paramount Merger Fight, Links Ellisons to Oracle's Israeli Military Ties
excerpt: The actor accused the Ellison family of using the Paramount-WBD merger to consolidate media power while profiting from military contracts in Gaza. Paramount called his remarks antisemitic.
body:
• Mark Ruffalo escalated his campaign against the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, explicitly linking CEO David Ellison's family to Oracle's contracts with the Israeli military.
  • Paramount fired back, calling Ruffalo's remarks "antisemitic" and saying the company does not "tolerate prejudice of any kind."
  • The $110 billion merger is currently on hold after a 12-state antitrust coalition sued in July 2026; a trial is expected in March 2027.
  • Over 4,000 industry professionals have signed an open letter opposing the merger, with Ruffalo and allies arguing that fear of retaliation is silencing dissent in Hollywood.

Actor Mark Ruffalo sharpened his attack on the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger this week, drawing a direct line between CEO David Ellison's family and Oracle's ties to the Israeli military — a move that triggered an immediate response from Paramount, which branded his remarks as antisemitic.

Ruffalo, who has been among the most vocal Hollywood critics of the deal, argued that the Ellison family's connections to both the Trump administration and Israel's military operations in Gaza make the merger a threat to editorial independence and democratic discourse.

"Today's news is a repudiation of Paramount's strategy of currying favor with the Trump administration to grease the wheels on this illegal merger — from sham settlement payments to manipulating its own news coverage," Ruffalo wrote on X in a recent post opposing the deal.

The Oracle Connection

David Ellison's father, Larry Ellison, co-founded Oracle and is one of the world's richest people. Larry Ellison has close ties to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and is a major donor to Friends of the IDF, a nonprofit that supports the Israeli military. Oracle, meanwhile, has technology contracts with the Israeli government.

https://x.com/Variety/status/2090956318462878136

Ruffalo and his allies have framed these connections as central to the merger's implications, arguing that consolidated media ownership under the Ellisons would extend their political influence across news networks including CBS and CNN's parent company.

Paramount pushed back forcefully. A statement from the studio called Ruffalo's characterization antisemitic and said the company "does not tolerate prejudice of any kind." The studio has previously maintained a do-not-hire list for talent it considers "overtly antisemitic," according to a report by Variety.

A Merger Under Siege

The clash comes as the $110 billion Paramount-WBD merger faces its most serious legal challenge yet. A 12-state coalition led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued on July 13 to block the deal, arguing it would violate federal antitrust law by reducing competition in cable and theatrical markets. Paramount agreed in late July not to close the deal until June 2027 or after a trial, whichever comes first.

"There are many reasons to block this deal, but we now believe the most fundamental one is what we encountered when asking artists to use their voices: fear. A deep, ugly and pervasive fear of speaking out."

— Mark Ruffalo and Matt Stoller, in a New York Times op-ed

Paramount has sought a $1.88 billion bond from the state attorneys general to cover the costs of delay, calling the lawsuit a threat to a deal that has been approved by regulatory entities in at least 68 countries.

South Asian Voices in the Debate

The boycott letter that helped spark the broader confrontation was signed by more than 4,000 film and television professionals, including British-Pakistani actor Riz Ahmed and Indian filmmaker Payal Kapadia. The entertainment industry's internal debate over political speech, artistic freedom, and corporate power has implications for South Asian creatives navigating Hollywood's evolving landscape.

What's Next

The antitrust trial is scheduled for March 2027. The Writers Guild of America has filed its own separate lawsuit against the merger. Meanwhile, Ruffalo and his "Block the Merger" coalition continue to push state attorneys general and members of Congress to intervene, arguing that the fight is about more than one deal — it is about who controls American media.
